verdict_text: YES. The script keys casting off an exact full-match pattern for the four projection matrices per layer (so embeddings, norms, biases and `wpe.weight` are untouched apart from a no-op `.float()` on already-float32 input), skips exactly the 12 `h.<i>.attn.bias` buffers, preserves names, asserts all four required checks before writing, and delegates the 64 MiB sharding plus index to `save_sharded_safetensors`. The unescaped `.` in the regexes is harmless here since no other key in the checkpoint would match those patterns, and `tensor.float().to(torch.bfloat16)` is bit-identical to `tensor.to(torch.bfloat16)` for float32 input.
